verdict.reasoning: Patient states feeling unwell for four days with sore throat and runny nose and now cough: "I've been feeling kind of under the weather for the past four days. It started with a sore throat and runny nose and it sort of... it's sort of going into a cough now."
Patient links onset to coworker sneezing: "It all started with the colleague of mine. She just kept sneezing next to me all the time."
Painful swallowing for one day: "Did you have any difficulty or pain on swallowing?" "Yeah, yeah, it was. It was quite painful to swallow... For one of the days."

Clear discharge and congestion: "Yeah, yeah, it's. It's clear, but sort of... getting my nose stuffed all the time. It's very hard to get it free." and clinician reflects "you feel quite congested" which patient agrees with.
Cough onset, type, and constancy: "that started recently, like just maybe yesterday. And it's. It's dry for now... but it's sort of there all the time."
Night sweats and tiredness: "I forgot to mention that I'm also having night sweats... And to the. Makes me a bit tired."

Earlier fever now improving with paracetamol and ibuprofen: "I had some fever in the beginning, but it's now sort of going down. I've been taking some paracetamol and I Bupren for that and they help."
Denies chest pain: "In terms of your chest, otherwise, have you any difficulty breathing or any pain in your chest?" "So no pain in the chest..."

Exertional dyspnea only: "I feel a bit winded on exertion..." and confirmed by clinician: "that's mainly on exercise, but when you're resting, there's no problem?" "Yeah, yeah. When I'm resting, it's okay."
Intermittent headaches: "Any headaches at all?" "Yeah, yeah, that's still there." and "they're not always there, but, you know, every now and then they would come and go."
Reduced appetite and increased fluids: "How's your appetite, sir?" "Yeah, I've been drinking a little bit more. More than the usual..." and "Maybe a bit less than what I would usually have."
Normal bowels and urination: "Tell me about your bowels. Are your bowels working okay?" "Yeah, yeah, I think so." and "Passing urine okay?" "Yeah, yeah."
Denies rashes: "Have you noticed any funny rashes at all on your skin?" "No. No."
Myalgias/joint aches: "any general muscle pain or aches? Joint pain?" "Yeah, yeah, That's. That's sort of started in the past couple days."

No past medical history: "Are you otherwise fitting well or do you have any other medical problems I should be aware of?" "So otherwise that I'm fine. There's. There isn't anything that I'm taking or I'm being treated for?"
OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen use: "I've been taking some paracetamol and I Bupren for that and they help." (context: for fever/temperature).
Plan to continue these medicines: "continuing with the regular paracetamol and ibuprofen, and we should see how things go."
No allergies: "Any allergies at all to any medications." "I should be aware Of, No."
Grandmother with type 2 diabetes: "Yeah, my grandma has diabetes." and "Do you know what type of diabetes it is?" "I think it's type two."
Lives alone: "Tell me, who do you live with at home?" "I live alone."
Works as accountant: "What do you do for work?" "I'm an accountant."
Occasional smoking: "in terms of smoking, do you smoke at all?" "Yeah, occasionally. No cigars and things on company parties."
Social alcohol: "And what about alcohol?" "Occasionally, I would have some. I'm not a very big drinker." and clinician: "Again, socially, with work."
Work stress reported: "How's your work going at the moment? Has it been affecting your work?" "A little bit?... it's a bit of a stressful period. Just around the end of the year."

Clinician assessment of viral URTI/flu-like illness with listed symptoms: "I think you probably have... a bit of a viral... upper respiratory tract infection or maybe early signs of a flu." plus summary: "last four days, you've been feeling generally quite unwell. Sore throat, runny nose, bit of a dry cough, bit of muscle pain, weakness, had an initial fever, but now settled." Headaches and congestion were also discussed earlier in the history.

Exertional dyspnea without rest dyspnea or chest pain is documented; linking it as likely from viral illness/fatigue is a reasonable clinical inference from the overall assessment of viral illness and lack of cardiopulmonary red flags.

Clinician explicitly downplays concern and mentions no red flags: "I don't think there's a lot to worry about. I think you probably have... a viral upper respiratory tract infection... It normally lasts for about seven to 10 days and just gets better..." and only advises return if worsening signs appear, implying stable condition and no current red flags.
Supportive care plan: "things you can do to really help yourself is get plenty of rest... pushing fluids and make yourself well hydrated, continuing with the regular paracetamol and ibuprofen."
Return next week if not better: "If next week you're still better, I want you to come back and see me." (context indicates if not better / still symptomatic).

Safety-net advice: "If you're really not getting better, if you have a high fever or your breathing is becoming a bit more labored, or chest pain, I'd like you to come back and see me much sooner. Give me a call and we can help you out."
No antibiotics are mentioned or prescribed; the clinician labels it viral and outlines only supportive measures, so absence of antibiotics is supported by the transcript.

Clinician explains typical 7–10 day course and to see how things go, with follow-up if not better: "It normally lasts for about seven to 10 days and just gets better..." and "If next week you're still better, I want you to come back and see me" plus earlier safety-netting if worsening.
Same as plan-002: "If next week you're still better, I want you to come back and see me." (intended as if still not better / still symptomatic).

Same safety-net statement: "If you're really not getting better, if you have a high fever or your breathing is becoming a bit more labored, or chest pain, I'd like you to come back and see me much sooner."
